_about: Frozen acceptance thresholds for ('mavic4pro', mesh revision 1), plan C.1-C.13. Written BEFORE the first acceptance run and not changed afterwards. Any later change must be logged in 'deviations' with its reason and needs user approval (plan C threshold freeze, critique M8).
rule: Every row is pass/fail on its own. 'report_only' rows are recorded and never gate. A threshold is never relaxed after seeing a result.
_what_was_known_when_this_file_was_writt: Every budget below that is a revision-0 number (slivers 87, repo buried defect 22.17 %, prop faces 3496, top-view IoU 0.3141) was measured on revision 0 alone before this file was written; none of them can be influenced by revision 1. The revision-1 mesh had already been built once when this file was written (its renders were needed for the C.10 visual review), so the following rows are declared rather than blind: C1_topology.components_per_group (an enumeration of the parts this builder adds), and C3_dimensions.targets[frame_width_no_props] (an arithmetic consequence of the frozen rotor xy and the measured can diameter). Neither is a tolerance that could be widened to make a failing number pass. This is stated here because plan M8 forbids choosing a threshold from a result.

C1_topology.sliver_budget_basis: mesh_check.check_mesh on revision 0's realized mavic4pro frame reports 87 slivers; revision 1 must not exceed it
C1_topology.components_basis: after drone_rev.finish_frame_assembly's per-group union: one body (shell + 4 arms + 4 motor pods, all overlapping), one can+adapter stack per rotor (4), one leg per FRONT motor (2), one battery solid, one PCB. The camera group holds 8 solids that do not touch each other: the gimbal head (block + lens barrel, unioned), six vision-sensor spheres seated on the shell, and the LiDAR. Revision 0's camera group holds 7 by the same count (its six sensors, LiDAR and gimbal, with two of them fused). Revision 1 has no 'canopy' group: its shell is one lofted surface, so revision 0's separate canopy dome does not exist.

C2_attachment.battery_clipped_rule: the pack keeps its official size; if it cannot fit with 1 mm clearance it is intersected with the shell and the clipped volume is logged (plan P8). A box clipped by more than half is no longer that battery and the component must be dropped.
C2_attachment.buried_plastic_definition: faces of a PLASTIC group (body, gear, canopy, accent) whose centroid lies inside ANOTHER PLASTIC solid, as a percentage of the shell group's surface area. This is the defect plan C.2 was written for: revision 0 swallows its own canopy.
C2_attachment.buried_plastic_in_camera_definition: plastic faces inside the camera solid, i.e. the nose around the gimbal. Gated against revision 0 rather than against 2 %, because the gimbal head IS partly inside the nose on this aircraft - the owned top photo shows the shell wrapping over the gimbal - and revision 0 buries 2601 of its 4030 camera faces (65 %) in the shell, so any improvement is an improvement on that.
C2_attachment.repo_buried_basis: mesh_check.check_buried_faces on revision 0 reports defect_pct 22.1655 (budget_pct 32.7); revision 1 must not be worse than revision 0
C2_attachment.C2b_basis: revision 0 has 88 prop triangles / 54 mm2 inside the motor bell (wf/mesh_inv_mini5pro.md, mavic4pro row), i.e. 1.55 % of the prop area budget used there; revision 1 must not be worse

official unfolded height, props excluded (DJI spec page and manual). This is the number the x1.59767 stretch exists to meet and the reason it is kept; B1's FCC fit puts the tallest resting feature at about 100 mm, so the model is about 35 mm taller than the photographs - see HEIGHT_SHORTFALL, reported as R-rows.

NOT the official 390.5 mm. It is the arithmetic consequence of two inputs this revision is not allowed to reconcile: plan B.0 freezes the rotor track at revision 0's 344.65 mm, while the measured can diameter is 29.33 mm, so 344.65 + 29.33 = 373.98 mm. Reaching the official 390.5 mm needs B1's measured front track 363.92 mm (363.92 + 29.33 = 393.25), which plan B.0 forbids changing. The 16.5 mm shortfall against the official number is reported, not gated.

C4_silhouette.metric: top-view silhouette IoU against the owned top photo (assets/photos/mavic4pro/mavic4pro_c02_arm_positions_topview_labelled.jpg), registered exactly as work/measure_planform.py established it (0.57912 mm/px, no rotation, origin at the rotor centroid). Nothing is re-fitted, so the IoU cannot be improved by moving the model. The photo mask is the light-grey airframe without the propellers; the model mask therefore also leaves out the prop, battery and pcb groups.
C4_silhouette.substitution_declared: plan C.4 names the FCC photos for this drone. The FCC plan views (p01, p07) are perspective-heavy and their rules lie on the table while the airframe stands about 100 mm above it, so the reference used here is the owned top photo the M4P-1 targets were measured on, with its scale anchored to B1's ruler-scaled FCC front track. Declared before the first run.
C4_silhouette.rev1_iou_min_rule: revision 0 + 0.05, the plan's own C.4 rule for this aircraft. No absolute floor is set: with the rotor xy frozen at revision 0's square 344.65 mm track while both owned readings give a trapezoid (front 363.9, rear 301.6-312.6 mm), the four arms are displaced 10-16 mm from the photo's, which is more than an arm width, so a large part of the union can never overlap. A floor would score that frozen constraint, not this build.
report_rows: top-view IoU restricted to |y| < 60 mm, i.e. the shell without the arms, for revision 0 and revision 1

C5_facing_area.what: one-sided facing area in 5 deg and 10 deg cones, by group and by material, at az 0/90/180 and el 0/-30/-90, revision 0 next to revision 1
C5_facing_area.why_report_only: plan C.5 sets ratio targets only for the Matrice 4E (against its CAD) and for the Phantom 4 camera. The Mavic 4 Pro has no owned CAD, so there is no value to compare a ratio with.

C6_facets.frame_faces_basis: the task's budget for this aircraft; revision 0 builds 17296
C6_facets.prop_faces_basis: revision 0 builds 3496 faces per rotor; plan B.1 says 'unchanged', and 3600 allows the P6 orientation change

C7_props.blade_angle_note: kept at the plan's value. The 2026-09-18 mini5pro round measured 0.43-0.50 deg on a P6 propeller and concluded no mesh that applies P6 can meet 0.2 deg, because what P6 changes IS the leading/trailing-edge assignment the chord angle measures. It is left unrelaxed here so the same finding is scored, not hidden.

C9_specular_census.what: specular foot census for revision 0 and revision 1 at the queue aspects, as a pre-registration input (plan D.0). It is an input to E3, not a gate on the geometry.

C10_visual.what: render sheet: revision 0 and revision 1 side by side plus the reference (top-photo overlay, FCC p05 front and p06 side). The builder writes notes per view and an independent agent re-reads the PNGs.

C11_certificates.mirror_symmetry_metric: (a) per-group mirrored area error, (b) |centre of mass y|, (c) per-group y bounding box symmetry. Mirrored-vertex distances are RECORDED for both revisions but do not gate - a vertex-level distance scores the triangulation, not the geometry (2026-09-18 mini5pro finding, adopted here before the first run rather than after it).
C11_certificates.note: src/mesh_symmetry.py and src/mesh_placement.py take a ledger census, not a mesh, so plan C.11 is implemented directly in benchmark/mesh_rev1_acceptance.py. Declared before the first run.

C12_material_table.what: area and volume per material group, revision 0 next to revision 1, and the group of every new part
C12_material_table.gate: every group must be a key of drones.DRONE_GROUP_MAT (no new material groups in a revision)
